panthera-tigris.delivery: Bundled GLB; one local viewer across behaviors
panthera-tigris.biology: Artist reconstruction. Taxonomic interpretation, shape and motion require expert review.
panthera-tigris.changes: Normalized original textured artist mesh and source skeleton retained; original run clip remains available. Solid atlas rendering uses depth-writing alpha cutouts. Independently authored v0.4.1 sit/rest/sleep postures separate carpal orientation from digit orientation, preserve limb lengths, raise the relaxed resting stifle, fold seated hocks/metatarsals and establish torso/forepaw support before limb contacts. Footfall trajectories and body anatomy remain unvalidated. Organic material metalness is zero. v0.4.4: slight supported torso lean in Sleep, independently authored source-atlas eyelid covers and closed margins attached to the existing head, and a quiet claw morph on the retained sixteen main artist claw components. Eyeball geometry, original texture/UVs and creator run remain intact; no photograph or raster is generated. Claw folding is an illustrative pose, not a modeled biological sheath or calibrated P3 joint. Forelimb dewclaws are missing from the source reconstruction. Camera fitting now uses actual visible posed vertices above the controls.

viewerRig.type: authored posture and facial attachments on original creator rig
viewerRig.author: PhenoVoxel Archive contributors
viewerRig.description: Same credited tiger across behaviors, with quieter paw/claw poses and an authored closed-eye Sleep posture. Sleep has a slight supported torso lean and lowered head; it does not simulate sleep physiology. The artist’s main claws fold dorsally in quiet poses, while forelimb dewclaws and sheath mechanics remain absent. Anatomy and motion need expert review.
viewerRig.scope: The original 47-joint artist skeleton, source surface, atlas, checksum and run clip remain unchanged. Added source-atlas eyelid covers follow the retained eyeballs/head, while a claw pose folds the sixteen artist claw components dorsally in quiet states. Claw targets are transformed back through the weighted bind-space skin matrices. Limb segment lengths and supported forepaw surfaces are retained. Eyelid/claw geometry, torso lean and timing are independently authored and unvalidated; forelimb dewclaws, sheath/P3 mechanics, forces and physiological sleep remain absent.
